mainEntity.name: What does a Web3 PR agency in the UAE actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: UAE-focused Web3 PR is about getting your project in front of MENA investors, VARA-licensed exchanges and the global press corps that covers the Gulf. That means pitching CoinDesk, The Block and Forbes with MENA-specific angles, timing campaigns around major Dubai events, and building media presence so AI engines cite you when a Gulf buyer asks about your category. A fractional senior operator like Shilika Jain does this directly for $5K–$12K/month.

acceptedAnswer.text: Full UAE-specialist agencies commonly charge $15K–$45K per month. A fractional senior operator with real MENA contacts runs the same senior scope for $5K–$12K per month. mainEntity.name: Which outlets and events matter for Web3 PR in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: For global tier-1 with MENA desks: CoinDesk Middle East, Cointelegraph, The Block. For mainstream: Forbes MENA, Arabian Business, Gulf Business. For regional crypto: Cryptonews Arabic, regional Telegram communities and Arabic-language YouTube. Key events to anchor campaigns around: TOKEN2049 Dubai (April), Future Blockchain Summit (October), GITEX Global (October).

mainEntity.name: What is the process and timeline for a UAE Web3 PR campaign?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks cover a teardown of your current press footprint and the narrative build: the regulatory angle, the three-sentence thesis and the journalist map. Weeks three and four cover embargo prep, media briefings and KOL alignment. Week five onwards is launch and compound coverage. For a token launch or fundraise announcement, six to twelve weeks of pre-launch build time is the minimum to get meaningful tier-1 placement rather than a wire blast.
